title: Migration 59 — the farmer policies stop refusing rows nobody meant to refuse
description: Three predicates on inventory_batches compared a nullable column against a literal, and RLS treats a NULL result as a refusal. `status` is nullable with no default, so a farmer creating a batch without naming one was rejected outright, and a farmer editing a batch whose stock_status was NULL got 0 rows changed and NO error -- the silent half. Measured on staging 2026-08-05, not inferred. The evidence that this is an oversight rather than a rule is the predicate's own inconsistency: it already spells the NULL case out for stock_status, twice, and never for status. The fixture stages the NULL-UNSAFE policies first, verbatim as production has them, because the substrate carries neither -- they come from two of the UNNUMBERED .sql files in the repo root, which no fixture applies and the coverage denominator cannot see. VERIFY proves both directions: the NULL cases are now admitted AND self-approval, self-publishing, admin-only lifecycle states and a rival's farm are all still refused. A migration that loosens a security policy and tests only the loosening would look green while handing a farmer the ability to approve their own stock. NOT read-only; wrapped in BEGIN..ROLLBACK.

verify.note: A asserts the premise (NULL <> 'Approved' is not TRUE) rather than assuming it. C and D are the two defects, and D asserts a ROW COUNT rather than catching an exception because the old behaviour raised nothing at all -- an exception handler would never have fired and the test would have passed while the bug remained. E is the counterweight: four things that must STILL be refused. The cross-farm gap this migration originally pinned in a section F is closed by migration 60; its proof moved there, so VERIFY 59 stays runnable against a database carrying both.
